narrative.coaching_note: The one change to make next time is to wash your hands with soap and water for 40 seconds instead of using the sanitizer bottle when C. difficile spores may be present. You touched bed rail A from 0.2 to 5.4 seconds, and contamination moved from bed rail A to bare hand at 0.2 seconds. That same contamination then moved to call button at 6.1 seconds and to resident A at 10.1 seconds. At 10.1 seconds you used alcohol rub from the sanitizer bottle for 29.9 seconds, which was long enough for a rub but alcohol does not kill C. difficile spores, so your bare hand stayed contaminated. That is why later contacts with resident A at 13.5 seconds and at 40 seconds were still exposures. Next time, use soap and water and the spores can be removed.
narrative.audit_summary: Analysis for C. difficile with source bed rail A. Transfers: bed rail A to bare hand at 0.2 seconds, to call button at 6.1 seconds, to resident A at 10.1 seconds, with additional resident A exposures at 13.5 and 40 seconds. No Moment 1, 2, 4, or 5 opportunities were identified (0 met / 0 opportunities), so no compliance rate applies and no moments were missed. One hygiene event at 10.1 seconds used alcohol rub for 29.9 seconds, which met WHO duration but is not effective against C. difficile spores; soap and water is required. No glove use issues were recorded. End contamination included bare hand, gloved hand, bed rail A, call button, and resident A. Disinfect resident A, bed rail A, and call button with an EPA List K sporicidal disinfectant effective against C. difficile spores.
